architecture_fit_summary: Preferred topology: single-tenant Private control plane in customer's account, inference runtime in customer VPC with private endpoints
Ingress: no public IPs; all inbound from internal app subnets via private ENIs through Transit Gateway
Egress: NAT Gateway to controlled egress subnets with static Elastic IPs; customer requires list of egress IPs for whitelist
Cross-region: primary in us-east-1, DR replica in eu-west-1; synchronous KV cache replication not required, async acceptable
Networking: recommend dedicated subnets per model-pool, route tables locked down, strict NACLs, and VPC Flow Logs enabled
Service connectivity: KMS CMK (customer-managed) via secure IAM role & cross-account access; HSM-backed key requested for prod
latency_throughput_targets: P99 latency < 120ms for reranking at 200 qps baseline; burst to 800 qps for market open; cost sensitivity medium-high (want tight control over token unit economics)
routing_needs: Prefer policy-driven routing: primary in-region model for latency, fallback to cheaper quantized variant on capacity pressure; explicit offline fallback for regulatory review traces
audit_kms_notes: Audit logs: Must ship inference telemetry + API call audit to customer's S3 bucket (encrypted) and to Splunk via Kinesis Firehose
Retention: Logs retained 7 years; access controls audited quarterly
KMS: Customer will provision CMK in their account; Redwood service principal to be granted Encrypt/Decrypt via IAM conditioned on source VPC
Key rotation: Customer requires annual rotation and proof-of-rotation in quarterly security reports
HSM: Prod KMS must be HSM-backed (FIPS 140-2) — pending procurement approval
notes: Key quote from Emma: 'We cannot expose raw customer data outside our tenant — every token and KV must live in our VPC.'
